rule_description: Internal employer category list: Category A (Govt/MNC/large listed) gets lowest rates; Category B (mid-size private) gets moderate rates; Category C (small firms) gets highest rates or rejection
Minimum income is Rs.15000 if salary account is with HDFC Bank; Rs.25000 for other bank accounts; Rs.50000 for non-HDFC salary account in some cases
Property ownership (own house vs rented) is a hidden scoring factor — own house improves eligibility
Geographic location of applicant is factored into eligibility score — metro applicants get better approval chances
Maximum loan = up to 27x net monthly salary (subject to max Rs.40 lakh)
SBI Xpress Credit (for salary account holders): min income Rs.25000; SBI Xpress Elite (select corporates only): higher loan amounts available
Xpress Elite scheme requires employer to be in SBI Select Corporate list or be a PSU/Government — unlisted private companies get lower loan limits
Minimum 6 months of salary credit history in bank account required — new account holders ineligible for best rates
Maximum loan = up to 24x net monthly salary subject to Rs.20 lakh cap
Minimum income is higher for metro cities — Rs.30000 in metros vs Rs.25000 in non-metro cities
Existing ICICI Bank account holders get preferential rates and lower minimum income threshold
Maximum 2 simultaneous personal loans allowed — requires high credit score and income
Self-employed: minimum 3 years business stability + Rs.15 lakh annual turnover + Rs.1 lakh profit after tax required
Minimum salary Rs.15000 for existing Axis Bank customers vs Rs.25000 for new customers — bank relationship reduces income threshold
FOIR below 40% gets lowest interest rate; 40-50% gets moderate rate; above 50% rejection
Corporate salary (listed MNC/PSU): min Rs.25000; Non-corporate salary (private unlisted): min Rs.30000; Kotak employees: min Rs.20000
Minimum salary varies by city: Rs.25001 in most cities; higher in metros like Mumbai/Delhi/Bangalore — exact city-wise list on website
Employer reputation is a scoring factor — top-tier employers get employees lower rates even at same income level
Applicants with lower total liabilities relative to income get higher loan amounts — not just FOIR but total debt picture
Minimum income varies by employer category: Tata Group employees Rs.15000; Category A (top MNC/PSU) Rs.20000; Category B Rs.25000; Category C (small firms) Rs.40000
FOIR cap is 75% (higher than most banks) — allows people with existing EMIs to still qualify
Maximum loan = up to 24x gross monthly income subject to Rs.20 lakh cap
Minimum income Rs.20000/month but may be flexible for rural applicants with good repayment history
Take-home salary after proposed EMI must be at least 30% of gross salary OR Rs.10000 — whichever is higher
Minimum gross salary Rs.15000 in other cities; Rs.20000 in Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Kolkata, Pune, Chennai, Ahmedabad
FOIR must be below 50% of monthly income — stricter than some private banks
Min CIBIL 710 for salaried applicants; Min CIBIL 760 for self-employed applicants — different thresholds by employment type
Applying to multiple banks simultaneously reduces approval chances — bank checks inquiry count in bureau report
Minimum income Rs.15000 in smaller cities; Rs.25000 in metro cities — city-based income threshold
EMIs allowed up to 65% of income — higher FOIR tolerance than most banks making it accessible for people with existing loans
Aadhaar card must be linked to mobile number — mandatory requirement not always listed prominently
Minimum family income Rs.25000/month even if individual salary is Rs.10000 — household income considered
Some sources indicate min CIBIL 750 (stricter than our 600 estimate) — varies by branch and loan amount
